headline: SPR Exchange Has a 25% Chance of Moving Crude
deck: U.S. DOE has solicited up to 17 million SPR barrels. This forecast settles on 31 December 2026, when an award-and-delivery record either exists or does not.
body: The U.S. Department of Energy has issued a request for proposals for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, Reuters reported. OilPrice.com separately reported that the department issued the RFP. [E1] [E2]
OilPrice.com said the solicitation is part of a U.S. commitment to make 172 million barrels available within an International Energy Agency emergency action of 400 million barrels. [E2]
DOE’s June announcement described a prior RFP that opened competitive bidding and continued the commitment within the wider IEA action. [E3]

DOE said the crude would come from Big Hill and Bryan Mound and that exchanges move supplies into the market to address short-term disruptions; it also said four previous solicitations awarded more than 133 million barrels across three completed exchanges and returned a 26% premium. [E4]

Curt Coccodrilli, DOE’s acting assistant secretary for the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office, said the exchange would move oil to refiners, ease short-term supply pressures and rebuild the reserve through premium barrels. [E5]
Under DOE’s exchange authority, participating companies return borrowed crude with additional premium barrels. [E6]
Plainview Energy reported that only 0.5 million barrels of the June offer were awarded, while describing an exchange as near-term borrowing that requires a later return plus a premium. [E7]
At the June RFP’s launch, Plainview Energy said near-term August oil traded at $90 a barrel and mid-2027 contracts at about $78, leaving a $5-per-barrel net margin after a 9% return premium. [E8]
By the bid deadline, Plainview Energy reported near-term crude at $80 a barrel while back-end prices held firmer, erasing the incentive it said marketers had to participate. [E9]

**The desk's reading.** The probability is 25% that this solicitation produces an award followed by a documented SPR crude delivery by 31 December 2026. The June result is the prior: the closest observed offer produced only a small award. The stronger competing reading is DOE’s record of completed exchanges, which keeps the call above near zero. Yet the current RFP’s bid terms, return obligation and economics are not in the record, so its cap is a ceiling rather than evidence of a flow. Since the paper’s 20 June coverage of oil movement through Hormuz, the question has shifted from a shipping corridor to whether this domestic exchange clears.

**The next test.** This call settles YES if, by 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2026, DOE publishes an award-and-delivery record for this solicitation identifying barrels that moved from the SPR; it settles NO if no such record is published by then. The award and delivery record distinguishes a clearing exchange from an unused ceiling.

confidence.label: DOE publishes an award-and-delivery record showing SPR crude moved under this solicitation by 23:59 UTC on 31 December 2026; otherwise NO.

Today’s solicitation opens competitive bidding, continuing DOE’s execution of President Trump’s 172-million-barrel release as part of a coordinated 400-million-barrel action by International Energy Agency (IEA) member nations’ strategic reserves.

source_note.raw_excerpt: These actions have moved critical crude oil supplies into the market to address short term supply disruptions and bolster energy security for the United States and its allies. The crude oil will originate from the SPR's Big Hill and Bryan Mound sites. This action builds on the Department’s four previous solicitations that collectively awarded more than 133 million barrels across three completed exchanges. DOE’s earlier exchanges demonstrated the SPR’s ability to rapidly deliver crude under emergency authorities while achieving a 26 percent premium in returned barrels.

source_note.raw_excerpt: “With today’s announcement, we are accelerating the President’s commitment to a coordinated and strategic release that stabilizes global oil markets,” said DOE Acting Assistant Secretary for the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office Curt Coccodrilli . “This exchange will help move oil swiftly to refiners, ease short-term supply pressures, and ensure the Strategic Petroleum Reserve continues to grow stronger through the return of premium barrels.”

source_note.raw_excerpt: Under DOE’s exchange authority, participating companies will return the 40 million borrowed barrels with additional premium barrels, ensuring immediate market supply while increasing the SPR’s long-term inventory. Bids for this solicitation are due no later than 11:00 A.M. Central Time on Monday, June 15, 2026.

evidence_box.fragment: Only 0.5 million barrels of the 40 million offered in June were awarded; marketers borrow near-term barrels and return them later with a premium.

source_note.raw_excerpt: The Department of Energy’s (DOE) June 10, 2026, Request for Proposal (RFP), which offered 40 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) sites at Bryan Mound and Big Hill, saw an incredibly weak market response. When the awards were finalized, only 0.5 million barrels of the 40 million offered were actually awarded to market participants. The current exchange program relies on a structure tailored heavily toward crude oil marketers, who borrow near-term barrels and agree to return them at a later date, along with an additional premium, essentially acting as interest paid in additional oil.
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim text from the source page.

evidence_box.fragment: At launch, near-term August oil traded at $90 per barrel while mid-2027 contracts sat around $78, creating a $5-per-barrel net margin after a 9% return premium.

source_note.raw_excerpt: When the RFP launched on June 10, near-term August oil contracts traded at $90 per barrel, while mid-2027 contracts sat around $78, creating an attractive $5 per barrel net profit margin for marketers even after factoring in the 9% return premium.
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim text from the source page.

evidence_box.fragment: By June 15, near-term crude prices fell to $80 while back-end prices held firmer, erasing the financial spread.

source_note.raw_excerpt: However, by the time bids were due on June 15, near-term crude prices collapsed to $80 per barrel while back-end prices held firmer (see graph below). This severe flattening of the curve completely erased the financial spread, leaving marketers with no financial incentive to participate in the exchange (see table below).

dissent.argument: I put the chance at 10%. The closest physical precedent awarded only 0.5 million of 40 million barrels, and the account attributes that result to the forward curve eliminating marketers’ incentive. The present record does not establish that the new bid terms or curve have changed enough to reverse that result. DOE’s completed exchanges show the machinery can work, but not that this solicitation will clear and produce documented movement by year-end.
